# #2023: Patch: the tests' must helper comes from the testkit, and the check keeps it so
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Sixty-two test files each define their own copy of the same three-line helper. It says "this card must be in the scenario" and fails the test with a message if it is not. Once this is built there is one copy, next to the other shared test helpers, and the repository's own check refuses a new one. Players see nothing; the code sheds about two hundred lines, and new card tests stop copying the helper.

## Why
- `grep -rnE 'fn must(<T>)?\(' crates | wc -l` gives 62:
  - 26 in card scripts' test modules, for example `crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c032_prem_panther.rs:70`, `c034_collateral_damage.rs:67` and `c035_lunar_eclipse.rs:75`;
  - 15 in `crates/cards/tests/cross`;
  - 17 in `crates/engine/tests/rules`, one of them already `pub` in `fixtures/prompt_harness.rs:80`;
  - 4 in `crates/server/tests`.
- Each takes an `Option<T>` (or `Option<CardInstance>`) and a label and returns `T`. They differ only in the panic text ("the scenario has no …", "missing: …", "expected …").
- #1978 and #2011 moved `unit_at`, `pick`, the fixtures and the act/live runners into the shared kits. They added rows to `SHARED_TEST_HELPERS` (`crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs:982-1022`) so that copies are refused. `must` is in no row.

## Proposal
- Add `pub fn must<T>(value: Option<T>, what: &str) -> T` to the engine's testkit, beside `unit_at` (`crates/engine/src/testkit/scenario.rs`). The card tests and the cross tests reach it through the `testkit` imports they already have.
- Delete the copies under `KIT_READERS` (`crates/engine/tests`, `crates/cards`, `crates/luau/tests`, `crates/ai/tests`).
  - That includes `prompt_harness.rs`'s copy, since two glob imports of one name clash.
  - The one-argument variant (`crates/cards/tests/cross/my_pawn.rs:543`) gets the label, or a name of its own.
- Add `"must"` to the `scenario.rs` row of `SHARED_TEST_HELPERS`.
- The 4 server copies move too, or stay as they are (the server tests are not kit readers). The PR says which.
- No call site changes.

## Where it lands
- `crates/engine/src/testkit/scenario.rs`
- the test modules of 26 card scripts under `crates/cards/src/scripts/`
- `crates/cards/tests/cross/`
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/`
- `crates/tools/tests/acceptance.rs`

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `grep -rnE 'fn must(<T>)?\(' crates/engine/tests crates/cards crates/luau/tests crates/ai/tests` finds nothing, and the testkit holds the one definition.
- [ ] The acceptance check refuses a `must` defined under a kit reader, as it does for the row's other names.
- [ ] `cargo test … -- --list` gives the same tests before and after for the engine's rules (with `testkit`), `jackioh-cards`' lib and its `cards` test.
- [ ] All of those pass, along with the tools' acceptance test, fmt and clippy.

## Size and risks
About 60 files, mechanical and test-only, apart from the testkit itself.

Risks:
- One small hunk in each of 26 card scripts, so it conflicts with any card PR open on one of them. It is a rebase, not a redesign.
- Editing the testkit turns on every `rust (test …)` group in CI.
- `acceptance.rs`'s table is a shared hot spot, so build this one at a time with the next suggestion (the rules tests' bench), not in parallel.

## Risks

- **Glob clashes.** If two globs bring different `must` items, every call is ambiguous and fails to compile.
  - After step 5, only `jackioh_engine::testkit` exports a `must`.
  - `jackioh_engine::prelude` has none, so a card's `mod tests` that globs both the prelude and the testkit still compiles.
  - Nested `mod base { use super::*; … }` modules pick it up through the parent's glob.
  - Do not add a `pub fn must` anywhere else.
- **A copy left behind** fails the acceptance test with its `path:line`. Delete that copy too; never narrow the scan.
- **Panic text.** The copies said "the scenario has no …", "missing: …" or "expected …". No test reads the message: the two `catch_unwind`s (`c099_craft_a_card.rs:473` and `c011_double_header.rs:268`) ignore it. So one message, `expected {what}`, is safe.
- **Merge conflicts** are likely with any open card PR on the 26 scripts, and with the next change to `acceptance.rs`'s table. Rebase; do not redesign.
- **CI cost.** Editing the testkit turns on every `rust (test …)` CI group.
- Determinism, replay, hidden information and the wire are untouched: only test code and docs change.
